title: Tool-call evaluation harness: selection accuracy & arg validation for regression monitoring
creator: Aisha Banerjee
description: Build an automated eval harness that measures tool/function-calling correctness (tool selection + argument validation) and ties those metrics to model/config changes so we can detect regressions during rollouts. The harness should be runnable as part of CI, produce per-commit and per-release dashboards, and emit alerts when critical thresholds are breached. Goals: 1) quantify tool selection accuracy across representative prompts and model variants; 2) validate argument types, required field presence, and semantic argument correctness; 3) surface regressions that are due to model changes, routing/config updates, or quantization profiles; 4) integrate with Console and rollout policies to support canary gating and automated fallback strategies.
acceptance_criteria: A synthetic and live prompt corpus covering top-50 tool use-cases is scoped and stored in evals repo
CI job 'toolcall-eval' runs on model/config PRs and returns a structured scorecard
Metrics emitted: tool_selection_accuracy, arg_precision, arg_recall, arg_type_error_rate, e2e_success_rate
Regression detection: alerts when tool_selection_accuracy drops >3% absolute or arg_recall drops >5% within a rollout window
Console shows drilldowns by model, quantization profile, and rollout cohort; PRs link to the scorecard and failing examples
steps: Design dataset schema for tool-call evaluation (labels: intended_tool, canonical_args, tolerances)
Implement evaluator module that runs a model + config against corpus and extracts predictions (tool id + serialized args)
Scoring pipeline: exact match, relaxed semantic match (type/coercion), and downstream validation via mini-sandbox where applicable
Integrate with CI to run on model artifact changes and config patches; publish artifacts to S3 and link in PR
Hook alerts into Console and PagerDuty for high-severity regression rules; wire into rollout gating logic
decision_log: 2026-02-22: Chose mixed synthetic + production-sampled prompts instead of only prod-samples to avoid PII leakage (decision by Aisha, Marcus, Priya)
2026-02-26: Use three-tier scoring (exact, typed/coerced, semantic) to balance strictness vs noise (agreed in eng-qa sync)
2026-03-03: Default regression thresholds set to 3% absolute for selection, 5% for arg recall; thresholds tunable per-customer (PM feedback)
2026-03-09: Chose to sandbox validate expensive tools (e.g., external API calls) via lightweight mocks to reduce cost and flakiness
comments: 2026-02-21 Marcus Li: Initial spike — prototyped evaluator that parses model toolcall JSON and computes exact-match on tool ids. Works for 80% of cases but arg normalization missing.
2026-02-24 Priya Nair (QA): Reviewed prototype, requested semantic matching for numeric types and date formats. Also flagged need for standardized arg schema across tools.
2026-03-01 Daniel Kim (PM): Add a column on the scorecard that shows which model/config change likely caused the regression (model vs routing vs quantization).
2026-03-08 Marcus Li: Implemented type-coercion layer and basic semantic matcher (Levenshtein for strings, tolerance for floats). Ran against 1k seeded examples; arg_recall improved from 72% -> 86%.
2026-03-11 Security: confirmed synthetic prompt corpus and prod-sample redaction approach acceptable for SOC review.
qa_notes: Include fuzzing of arg orders and extra unexpected keys to ensure resilient deserialization
Add a small production-sampled set (n=200) that is redacted and re-run weekly to keep coverage realistic
Label known flaky tool connectors and exclude from blocking alerts until connector fixes are implemented
risks_and_mitigations: False positives from loose semantic matching: mitigate by exposing per-check confidence and allowing per-customer thresholds
Compute cost of large eval runs: provide fast 'smoke' subset for CI and scheduled nightly full runs
Drift in allowed arg formats across tool updates: enforce tool schema registry and backward-compatible validators
